transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, it's probably not a huge deal... but I've been having a little trouble with, well, snacking, I guess you could call it. Late at night. 

What worries me—and it's a bit embarrassing to admit—is that once I start picking at the food, I'll tell myself, 'That's enough, Santiago,' but... my hand just keeps going back. It's almost like I don't get to make the decision anymore. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay for you.
Can you describe what happens after you start eating? Do you feel like you can stop if you want to, or does it feel like you lose control once you begin?

Well, um, it's a little hard to explain, but... yeah, it's kind of like I lose control, I guess. I mean, I know I shouldn't keep eating, and I'll literally say to myself, "Okay, Santiago, that's enough," but then... my hand just keeps going back to the food. It's like I'm not the one making the choice to keep eating, even though I know I am. It's silly, isn't it? I should be able to just stop, but... I don't know, does that make sense to you? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Does this loss of control around eating cause you distress, or has it affected other areas of your life, like your work, relationships, or how you see yourself?

Oh, well, um... I really don't want to make it sound like some huge crisis. It's not ruining my life or anything. I'm still getting to all my shipping and receiving shifts, and I'm handling all my responsibilities at work just fine. I make sure of that, so you don't have to worry there. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it does bother me a little bit at home. I've actually started, well, kind of avoiding some of that late family time when everyone is hanging out in the kitchen. I just... I get worried someone will notice how uneasy I am around the food, and I really don't want them to think poorly of me or cause a fuss. Is that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
When you're eating during these episodes, do you find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or eating a lot even when you're not really hungry?

Well, um... I guess I do eat even when my stomach isn't actually grumbling. It's more of a habit, maybe? But, um, to answer your question about feeling full... I try not to let it get too out of hand, I really do. But sometimes, by the time I finally stop, my stomach does feel a bit... tight and heavy. 

It's nothing serious, just, you know, I usually have to sit on the edge of the couch for a little while afterward. Bending over or lying down just feels a bit uncomfortable when I get like that. I hope that's not too unusual? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can for you, so I hope that's the kind of detail you were looking for.
